title: Ares Alpha baseline viability
statement: Under the current EXP-CIV-001 baseline model and seed, Ares Alpha remained viable for 365 Sols while material reserves, technology, and CQ increased together; this is provisional evidence that material resilience and coordinated capability can reinforce one another in the current CivilOS model.
evidence: results/exp-civ-001/baseline-001.json records a completed 365-Sol run with 365 observations.
Population remained at 20 throughout the run and no configured failure signal was met.
The minimum observed energy, water, and food values were 82.8, 79.1, and 91.6 respectively.
Technology increased from 34.89 to 100.0 and CQ increased from 0.42 to 1.0.
All five configured success signals were met in the deterministic baseline report.
limitations: This insight is based on one deterministic baseline configuration and one seed; it is not yet a cross-scenario conclusion.
Energy, water, food, technology, and CQ approach or reach model ceilings, suggesting the current baseline may be too forgiving to measure long-run trade-offs well.
Population remained flat, so the run does not yet test demographic growth, decline, or replacement dynamics.
Several event types repeat on a fixed five-Sol cycle, limiting the diversity and realism of shocks.
The current signal evaluator is rule-based and should not be treated as independent scientific validation.
implications: The baseline is useful as a deterministic control case for future comparison experiments.
The next experiments should vary resource margins, event severity, profession composition, and institutional/CQ conditions rather than treating this baseline result as validated truth.
Ceiling saturation should be reduced or stress scenarios introduced before drawing stronger conclusions about sustainability.
decision_relevance: Use EXP-CIV-001 baseline-001 as the control run for Ares Alpha experiment design.
Do not promote this insight beyond provisional status until comparison runs reproduce or challenge the pattern.
Prioritize stress-test and sensitivity experiments before using Ares Alpha findings in YICE or real-world decision guidance.
